claim.quote: The results show no excess in the reactor-on data, reaching the world record sensitivity down to recoil energies of about 1 keV (0.1 keV electron-equivalent).

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published Phys. Rev. D 100, 092005 (2019).

key_value_text.quote: A 95% confidence level limit for new physics is established at an event rate of 40 times the one expected from the standard model at this energy scale.
key_value_text.value: 95% CL limit for new physics at an event rate of 40 times the one expected from the Standard Model

name: Exploring low-energy neutrino physics with the Coherent Neutrino Nucleus Interaction Experiment (CONNIE)

significance.quote: A 95% confidence level limit for new physics is established

summary.plain: The first results from the upgraded CONNIE detector found no excess of events when the reactor was on, reaching the best sensitivity then achieved at reactors for nuclear recoils near one keV, and limiting new physics to about 40 times the Standard Model rate.
summary.technical: 8 CCDs, 47.6 g active mass at 30 m from the 3.8 GW_th Angra 2 core: reactor-on 2.1 kg-day vs reactor-off 1.6 kg-day, no excess; 95 % CL limit on new physics at 40 times the Standard Model CEvNS rate near 1 keV.

title: Exploring low-energy neutrino physics with the Coherent Neutrino Nucleus Interaction Experiment (CONNIE)
why_it_matters: Demonstrated that CCDs reach the sub-keV thresholds needed for reactor CEvNS.
